Source: The patient initially denied medical treatment but his wife convinced him to be taken by ambulance to the emergency department for evaluation.
The paramedics report that at the scene the patient had a Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) of 15.
A 54-year-old man is brought to the emergency department following a skiing accident.
His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, and a prior transient ischemic attack.
When he woke up, he was mildly confused but able to ski down the rest of the mountain.
In the emergency department, his temperature is 97.8°F (36.6°C), blood pressure is 141/84 mmHg, pulse is 71/min, and respirations are 16/min.
During the ride, he became gradually more somnolent.
He is difficult to arouse with a GCS of 7.
His medications include atorvastatin and lisinopril.
A head CT is performed and can be seen in Figure A.
He lost consciousness for about 30 seconds.
The patient lost control of his skis and collided with a tree.
